newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Greece sends bullet-proof vests to Albania police.
newsitem.headline: Greece sends bullet-proof vests to Albania police.

text.p: Greece on Thursday sent chaotic Albania bullet-proof jackets, vehicles, uniforms and other equipment to help police in the capital Tirana and the troubled port of Vlore.
A Greek ship unloaded the equipment at the port of Durres, 50 km (30 miles) west of Tirana, and was met by deputy interior minister Ndre Legisi, Albania's state-run news agency ATA reported.
"We are really grateful to the Greek government for both moral support and the important equipment they have provided us with," Legisi said after welcoming the ship in Durres.

Albanian police are struggling against organised crime and armed gangs which mushroomed in March when violence and lawlessness swept Europe's poorest nation following the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.

Rival armed gangs battle almost daily in Vlore, the birthplace of the unrest against the Democratic Party government in March. The Democrats lost a general election to their rival Socialists and their allies last month.
More than 1,500 people were killed in more than four months of violence and an estimated one million guns, looted from police and army depots, remain in private hands or in the possession of gangs.
